title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第十: 張儉 邢抱朴 馬得臣 蕭朴 耶律八哥
title.en: Volume 80 Biographies 10: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, Yelu Eight Brothers
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第十: 張儉 邢抱朴 馬得臣 蕭朴 耶律八哥 Volume 80 Biographies 10: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, Yelu Eight Brothers

sentences.zh: 張儉邢抱樸馬得臣蕭樸耶律八哥

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, Yelu Bagge
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, Xing Baopu, Ma Dechen, Xiao Pu, and Yelu Bagge

sentences.zh: 張儉，宛平人，性端愨，不事外飾。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian was a man of Wanping; his nature was upright and sincere, and he did not pursue outward adornment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, a native of Wanping, was by nature upright and sincere and did not cultivate outward display.

sentences.zh: 統和十四年，舉進士第一，調雲州幕官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he took first place in the jinshi examination and was assigned as a staff officer in Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he placed first among jinshi graduates and was posted as a staff officer in Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 故事，車駕經行，長吏當有所獻。

translations.literal: By established precedent, when the imperial carriage passed through, the chief local official was obliged to present something.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, whenever the imperial carriage passed through a region, the chief local official was expected to present a tribute.

sentences.zh: 聖宗獵雲中，節度使進曰：「臣境無他產，惟幕僚張儉，一代之寶，願以為獻。」

translations.literal: When Shengzong hunted in Yunzhong, the military commissioner advanced and said: "Within my jurisdiction there is no other product; only my staff officer Zhang Jian, a treasure of a generation — I wish to present him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzong was hunting in Yunzhong, the military commissioner came forward and said, "My territory has no other notable product to offer; only my staff officer Zhang Jian, a treasure of his age — I wish to present him to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 先是，上夢四人侍側，賜食人二口，至聞儉名，始悟。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had dreamed of four men attending at his side and of two mouths given food to eat; when he heard Jian's name, he understood at last.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had dreamed of four men standing at his side and of two mouths being given food; when he heard Jian's name, he understood the omen at last.

sentences.zh: 召見，容止樸野。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, his bearing and manner were rustic and plain.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience, his bearing and manner were plain and unadorned.

sentences.zh: 訪及世務，占奏三十餘事。

translations.literal: Asked about affairs of the age, he submitted advisories on more than thirty matters.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned on affairs of the day, he presented memorials on more than thirty topics.

sentences.zh: 由此顧遇特異，踐歷清華，號稱明幹。

translations.literal: From this his favor was exceptionally marked; he ascended through exalted offices and was acclaimed as clear-sighted and capable.
translations.idiomatic: From this his favor was singular; he rose through the highest offices and was acclaimed as clear-sighted and capable.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，累遷同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the Kaitai era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy director of the Commission for Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaitai era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy director of the Commission for Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太平五年，出為武定軍節度使，移鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping he went out as military commissioner of the Wuding Army and was transferred to command at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping he was appointed military commissioner of the Wuding Army and later transferred to command at Datong.

sentences.zh: 六年，入為南院樞密使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered court as Southern Academy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to court as commissioner of the Southern Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷倚，參知政事吳叔達與儉不相能，帝怒，出叔達為康州刺史，拜儉左丞相，封韓王。

translations.literal: The Emperor was just then relying on him heavily; Participating State Counselor Wu Shuda could not get along with Jian; the Emperor in anger sent Shuda out as prefect of Kangzhou, appointed Jian left chief councilor, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then leaning heavily on him; Participating State Counselor Wu Shuda could not work with Jian, and the Emperor in anger sent Shuda out as prefect of Kangzhou, appointed Jian left chief councilor, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，受遺詔輔立太子，是為興宗，賜貞亮弘靖保義守節耆德功臣，拜太師、中書令，加尚父，徙王陳。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, he received the final edict to assist in establishing the heir — this was Xingzong — and was granted the title of meritorious minister preserving loyalty and aged virtue; he was appointed Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, raised to Honored Father, and transferred to Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill, Jian received the deathbed edict to assist in establishing the heir, who became Xingzong; he was granted the title of meritorious minister of steadfast integrity and aged virtue, appointed Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, raised to Honored Father, and transferred to Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 重熙五年，帝幸禮部貢院及親試進士，皆儉發之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongxi the Emperor visited the Board of Rites examination hall and personally tested jinshi candidates; all of this was initiated by Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongxi the Emperor visited the Board of Rites examination compound and personally tested jinshi candidates — reforms that Jian had proposed.

sentences.zh: 進見不名，賜詩褒美。

translations.literal: On entering audience his name was not called aloud; he was granted a poem in praise.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to audience his name was not announced aloud, and the Emperor granted him a poem of praise.

sentences.zh: 儉衣唯紬帛，食不重味，月俸有餘，赒給親舊。

translations.literal: Jian wore only plain silk; his food had no duplicated flavors; when his monthly salary had a surplus he gave it to relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jian wore only plain silk, took no dish with duplicated flavors at his table, and when his monthly salary had a surplus he gave it to relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 方冬，奏事便殿，帝見衣袍弊惡，密令近侍以火夾穿孔記之，屢見不易。

translations.literal: In midwinter, while reporting on business in the side hall, the Emperor saw his robes and cloak worn and shabby; he secretly ordered attendants to burn holes with fire-tongs as markers; he saw them again and again yet Jian did not change them.
translations.idiomatic: One winter, while Jian was reporting on business in the side hall, the Emperor noticed his robe and cloak were worn and shabby; he secretly ordered attendants to burn marker holes in them with fire-tongs, yet saw them again and again unchanged.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，儉對曰：「臣服此袍已三十年。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; Jian replied: "Your servant has worn this robe for thirty years already.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked why; Jian replied, "Your servant has worn this robe for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 時尚奢靡，故以此微諷喻之。

translations.literal: At the time extravagance was fashionable, so he used this as a subtle parable.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance was then in fashion, and he meant this as a subtle admonition.

sentences.zh: 上憐其清貧，令恣取內府物，儉奉詔持布三端而出，益見獎重。

translations.literal: The Emperor, pitying his poverty, ordered him to take whatever he wished from the inner treasury; Jian received the edict, took only three bolts of cloth, and went out — and was esteemed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, pitying his poverty, told him to take whatever he wished from the inner treasury; Jian obeyed the edict, took only three bolts of cloth, and left — and was esteemed all the more.

sentences.zh: 儉弟五人，上欲俱賜進士第，固辭。

translations.literal: Jian had five younger brothers; the Emperor wished to grant them all jinshi degrees, but Jian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had five younger brothers; the Emperor wished to grant them all jinshi degrees, but Jian firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 有司獲盜八人，既戮之，乃獲正賊。

translations.literal: The authorities apprehended eight robbers, executed them, and only afterward captured the real culprit.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities seized eight robbers, executed them, and only afterward captured the real culprit.

sentences.zh: 家人訴冤，儉三乞申理。

translations.literal: The families lodged a grievance of injustice; Jian three times begged that the case be reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: The families appealed that they had been wronged; Jian three times begged that the case be reviewed.

sentences.zh: 上勃然曰：「卿欲朕償命耶！」

translations.literal: The Emperor flared up and said: "Do you wish that We repay lives!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flared up and said, "Do you wish that We repay lives with lives!

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「八家老稚無告，少加存恤，使得收葬，足慰存沒矣。」

translations.literal: Jian said: "The eight households, old and young, have no one to plead for them; if Your Majesty would only show a little care and relief so that they could collect the bodies for burial, that would be enough to comfort the living and the dead."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "The eight households, young and old, have no one to plead for them; if Your Majesty would show a little care so they could gather the bodies for burial, that would be enough to comfort both the living and the dead."

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then acceded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then granted his request.

sentences.zh: 儉在相位二十餘年，裨益為多。

translations.literal: Jian held the chief minister's seat for more than twenty years and contributed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Jian held the chief minister's post for more than twenty years and contributed greatly to the state.

sentences.zh: 致政歸第，會宋書辭不如禮，上將親征。

translations.literal: Having retired from office and returned to his residence, it happened that Song's letter of reply was not in proper form; the Emperor was about to launch a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring from office and returning home, it happened that Song's diplomatic reply was not in proper form; the Emperor was about to lead a campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 幸儉第，尚食先往具饌，卻之；

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Jian's mansion; the imperial kitchen went ahead to prepare a feast, but Jian declined it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited Jian's house; the imperial kitchen went ahead to prepare a feast, but Jian declined it.

sentences.zh: 進葵羹幹飯，帝食之美。

translations.literal: He served sunflower broth and dried rice; the Emperor ate it and found it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: He served sunflower broth and plain dried rice; the Emperor ate it and pronounced it excellent.

sentences.zh: 徐問以策，儉極陳利害，且曰：「第遣一使問之，何必遠勞車駕？」

translations.literal: The Emperor gradually asked his counsel on policy; Jian expounded at length on advantage and harm, and said: "Why not simply send an envoy to inquire? Why must the imperial carriage be troubled to go so far?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gradually questioned him on policy; Jian set forth at length the advantages and harms, and said, "Why not simply send an envoy to inquire? Why trouble the imperial carriage to go so far?

sentences.zh: 上悅而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and stopped the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and abandoned the campaign.

sentences.zh: 復即其第賜宴，器玩悉與之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again came to his mansion to grant a feast; vessels and curios were all given to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again came to his house to grant a feast and gave him all the vessels and curios used there.

sentences.zh: 二十二年薨，年九十一，敕葬宛平縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged ninety-one; an edict ordered burial in Wanping county.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of his tenure he died, aged ninety-one; an edict ordered his burial in Wanping county.

sentences.zh: 邢抱樸，應州人，刑部郎中簡之子也。

translations.literal: Xing Baopu was a man of Ying Prefecture and the son of Xing Jian, director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Baopu, a native of Ying Prefecture, was the son of Xing Jian, director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 抱樸性穎悟，好學博古。

translations.literal: Baopu was by nature quick and perceptive, fond of study, and broad in ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Baopu was quick-witted by nature, devoted to study, and broad in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 保寧初，為政事舍人、知制誥，累遷翰林學士，加禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoning he served as drafting academician for political affairs and edicts, was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin academician, and was given the additional title of vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoning he served as drafting academician for political affairs and edicts, rose through repeated promotions to Hanlin academician, and was given the additional title of vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 統和四年，山西州縣被兵，命抱樸鎮撫之，民始安，加戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when western Shanxi prefectures and counties suffered from warfare, Baopu was ordered to pacify the region; the people first knew security; he was made minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tonghe, when the prefectures and counties of western Shanxi were ravaged by war, Baopu was ordered to pacify them; the people first regained security, and he was made minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士承旨，與室昉同修《實錄》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin academician director and, with Shi Fang, jointly compiled the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician director and, with Shi Fang, jointly compiled the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 決南京滯獄還，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: After adjudicating long-pending cases at Nanjing and returning, he received a gracious edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: After settling long-pending cases at Nanjing and returning, he received a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed participating state counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed participating state counselor.

sentences.zh: 以樞密使韓德讓薦，按察諸道守令能否而黜陟之，大協人望。

translations.literal: On recommendation of commissioner Han Derang, he inspected prefectural and county magistrates throughout the circuits for competence and promoted or demoted them; this accorded greatly with popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Commissioner Han Derang, he inspected magistrates throughout the circuits for competence and promoted or dismissed them accordingly; this accorded greatly with public expectation.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去官，詔起視事。

translations.literal: Before long, on his mother's death he left office; an edict recalled him to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on his mother's death he left office, but an edict recalled him to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 表乞終制，不從；

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to complete mourning rituals; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to complete the full mourning period; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 宰相密諭上意，乃視事。

translations.literal: The chief councilors secretly conveyed the Emperor's mind, and only then did he resume office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilors privately conveyed the Emperor's wishes, and only then did he resume office.

sentences.zh: 人以孝稱。

translations.literal: People acclaimed him for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: People praised him for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及耶律休哥留守南京，又多滯獄，復詔抱樸平決之，人無冤者。

translations.literal: When Yelü Xiuge held Nanjing in garrison and again had many cases in arrears, an edict once more ordered Baopu to settle them; no one remained wronged.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelü Xiuge held Nanjing in garrison and again accumulated many cases in arrears, an edict once more ordered Baopu to settle them, and no one was left wronged.

sentences.zh: 改南院樞密使，卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Southern Academy commissioner; he died and was posthumously granted palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Southern Academy; he died and was posthumously granted the title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，抱樸與弟抱質受經於母陳氏，皆以儒術顯，抱質亦官至侍中，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Baopu and his younger brother Baozhi had received the classics from their mother, Lady Chen; both rose to eminence through Confucian learning; Baozhi also reached the post of palace attendant; men of the time took pride in them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Baopu and his younger brother Baozhi had studied the classics under their mother, Lady Chen; both rose to prominence through Confucian learning, and Baozhi also reached the post of palace attendant; men of the time took pride in the family.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀房玄齡、杜如晦，隋季書生，向不遇太宗，安能為一代名相？

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui — bookish men of the Sui season — how could they have become famous ministers of a generation had they not met Taizong?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui — mere scholars of the late Sui — who could never have become the great ministers of an age had they not met Emperor Taizong?

sentences.zh: 臣雖不才，陛下在東宮，幸列侍從，今又得侍聖讀，未有裨補聖明。

translations.literal: Though I am without talent, when Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace I was fortunate to rank among your attendants; now again I attend your sacred readings; I have as yet made no contribution to Your Majesty's enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am without talent, when Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace I was fortunate to serve among your attendants; now again I attend your sacred readings, yet I have made no contribution to Your Majesty's enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗問臣以貞觀、開元之事，臣請略陳之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once questioned me about the reigns of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan; I beg leave to set them forth briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once asked me about the reigns of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan; I beg leave to set them forth briefly.

sentences.zh: 臣聞唐太宗侍太上皇宴罷，則挽輦至內殿；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Emperor Taizong of Tang attended the Supreme Emperor at banquet's end, he would draw the carriage to the inner hall;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that after banquets with the retired emperor, Emperor Taizong of Tang would draw the imperial carriage himself to the inner hall;

sentences.zh: 玄宗與兄弟歡飲，盡家人禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong drank merrily with his brothers and fulfilled all the rites of family.
translations.idiomatic: and that Emperor Xuanzong drank merrily with his brothers and observed all the rites of kinship within a family.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣祖考之祚，躬侍太后，可謂至孝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has inherited the throne of your ancestors and in person attends the Empress Dowager — this may be called utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited the throne of your forefathers and in person attends the Empress Dowager — this may truly be called utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 臣更望定省之餘，睦六親，加愛敬，則陛下親親之道，比隆二帝矣。

translations.literal: Your servant further hopes that beyond morning and evening attendance, Your Majesty will harmonize the six kin, increase love and respect, and then Your Majesty's way of cherishing kin will equal the elevation of those two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further hopes that beyond your daily attendance, Your Majesty will bring harmony among the six degrees of kin, increase love and respect among them, and then Your Majesty's devotion to kin will rival that of those two emperors.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞二帝耽玩經史，數引公卿講學，至於日昃。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the two emperors were absorbed in the classics and histories, repeatedly summoning dukes and ministers to lecture on learning, even until the sun slanted west.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that those two emperors were absorbed in the classics and histories, repeatedly summoning dukes and ministers to lecture on learning until the sun had passed the meridian.

sentences.zh: 故當時天下翕然向風，以隆文治。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time the realm turned as one toward their influence, and literary governance was elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the realm at that time turned as one toward their example, and civil governance flourished.

sentences.zh: 今陛下遊心典籍，分解章句，臣願研究經理，深造而篤行之，二帝之治，不難致矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's mind roves in the canonical texts and you parse passages and clauses; your servant wishes to study statecraft in depth, pursue it further, and practice it steadfastly — the governance of the two emperors would not be hard to attain.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's mind dwells in the canonical texts and you parse passages and clauses; your servant wishes to study statecraft in depth, pursue it further, and practice it steadfastly — the governance of those two emperors would not be hard to attain.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞太宗射豕，唐儉諫之；

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that when Taizong shot at a boar, Tang Jian remonstrated with him;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that when Taizong shot at a boar, Tang Jian remonstrated with him;

sentences.zh: 玄宗臂鷹，韓休言之；

translations.literal: when Xuanzong carried a hawk on his arm, Han Xiu spoke of it;
translations.idiomatic: when Xuanzong carried a hawk on his arm, Han Xiu spoke against it;

sentences.zh: 二帝莫不樂從。

translations.literal: and neither of the two emperors failed to follow with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: and both emperors gladly accepted their counsel.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以球馬為樂，愚臣思之，有不宜者三，故不避斧鉞言之：竊以君臣同戲，不免分爭，君得臣愧，彼負此喜，一不宜。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty takes ball and horse for pleasure; your foolish servant reflects on this and finds three points of impropriety; therefore I do not avoid the axe and halberd in speaking: I venture to think that when ruler and minister play together, contention cannot be avoided — the ruler wins and the minister is shamed, one side loses and the other rejoices — the first impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty takes pleasure in ball games and horsemanship; your foolish servant has reflected on this and finds three improprieties, and therefore speaks though it may cost his life: when ruler and minister play together, contention cannot be avoided — the ruler wins and the minister is shamed, one side loses and the other rejoices — the first impropriety.

sentences.zh: 躍馬揮杖，縱橫馳騖，不顧上下之分，爭先取勝，失人臣禮，二不宜。

translations.literal: Leaping horses and brandishing sticks, galloping freely in every direction, heedless of the distinction between superior and inferior, striving to win first — this loses the rites of a minister toward his ruler; the second impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Leaping horses and brandishing mallets, galloping freely without regard for the distinction between superior and inferior, striving to win — this violates the rites owed by a minister to his ruler; the second impropriety.

sentences.zh: 輕萬乘之尊，圖一時之樂，萬一有銜勒之失，其如社稷、太后何？

translations.literal: To treat lightly the dignity of the ten-thousand chariots and seek a moment's pleasure — if by any chance there should be a mishap with bridle or reins, what of the altars of state and the Empress Dowager?
translations.idiomatic: To treat lightly the dignity of the Son of Heaven and seek a moment's pleasure — if by any chance there should be an accident with bridle or reins, what would become of the altars of state and the Empress Dowager?

sentences.zh: 三不宜。

translations.literal: The third impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: The third impropriety.

sentences.zh: 儻陛下不以臣言為迂，少賜省覽，天下之福，群臣之願也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not regard your servant's words as impractical and will grant them a little consideration, it will be the fortune of the realm and the wish of all your ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not regard your servant's words as impractical and will grant them a little consideration, it will be the fortune of the realm and the wish of all your ministers.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝嘉嘆良久。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised and sighed over it for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it and sighed over it for a long while.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，贈太子太保，詔有司給葬。

translations.literal: Before long he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to provide burial.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to provide for his burial.

sentences.zh: 蕭樸，字延寧，國舅少父房之族。

translations.literal: Xiao Pu, style name Yanning, was of the clan of the empress's father's younger branch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Pu, style name Yanning, belonged to the clan of the empress's father's younger branch.

sentences.zh: 父勞古，以善屬文為聖宗詩友。

translations.literal: His father Laogu, being skilled in literary composition, was Shengzong's companion in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Laogu, skilled in literary composition, was Shengzong's companion in poetry.

sentences.zh: 樸幼如老成人。

translations.literal: Pu in youth was like a seasoned adult.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Pu was grave and mature like an old man.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學多智。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and full of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and full of resource.

sentences.zh: 開泰初，補牌印郎君，為南院承旨，權知轉運事，尋改南面林牙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaitai he was appointed seal-and-plaque gentleman, served as Southern Academy director, was given acting charge of transport affairs, and soon was transferred to Southern Face linya.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaitai he was appointed seal-and-plaque gentleman, served as director of the Southern Academy, was given acting charge of transport affairs, and soon was transferred to Southern Face linya.

sentences.zh: 帝問以政，樸具陳百姓疾苦，國用豐耗，帝悅曰：「吾得人矣！」

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned him on government; Pu set forth in detail the people's hardships and whether state revenue was abundant or depleted; the Emperor said with pleasure: "I have found my man!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned him on government; Pu set forth in detail the people's hardships and whether state revenue was abundant or depleted; the Emperor said with pleasure, "I have found my man!

sentences.zh: 擢左夷離畢。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left yilibi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left yilibi.

sentences.zh: 時蕭合卓為樞密使，樸知部署院事，以酒廢事，出為興國軍節度使，俄召為南面林牙。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Hezhuo was commissioner; Pu managed Deployment Court affairs; because of wine he neglected his duties and was sent out as military commissioner of the Xingguo Army; before long he was recalled as Southern Face linya.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Hezhuo was commissioner; Pu managed Deployment Court affairs; because drink caused him to neglect his duties, he was sent out as military commissioner of the Xingguo Army, but before long he was recalled as Southern Face linya.

sentences.zh: 太平三年，守太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping he served as guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping he served as guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜北府宰相，遷北院樞密使。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Northern Prefecture chief councilor and transferred to Northern Academy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed chief councilor of the Northern Prefecture and promoted to commissioner of the Northern Academy.

sentences.zh: 時太平日久，帝留心翰墨，始畫譜牒以別嫡庶，由是爭訟紛起。

translations.literal: Peace had then lasted long; the Emperor turned his mind to brush and ink, and for the first time drew up genealogical registers to distinguish legitimate from secondary lines; from this lawsuits arose in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had then lasted long; the Emperor turned his attention to records and genealogy, and for the first time drew up registers to distinguish legitimate from secondary lines; from this lawsuits arose in profusion.

sentences.zh: 樸有吏才，能知人主意，敷奏稱旨，朝議多取決之。

translations.literal: Pu had talent for administration; he could grasp the ruler's intent; his presentations accorded with the Emperor's wishes; court deliberations often took his word as decisive.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had administrative talent; he could grasp the ruler's intent; his presentations accorded with the Emperor's wishes; and court deliberations often followed his judgment.

sentences.zh: 封蘭陵郡王，進王恒，加中書令。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling commandery, advanced to Prince of Heng, and given the additional title of Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling, advanced to Prince of Heng, and given the additional title of Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 及大延琳叛，詔安撫東京，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When Dazhonglin rebelled, an edict ordered him to pacify the Eastern Capital, acting at his discretion as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When Dazhonglin rebelled, an edict ordered him to pacify the Eastern Capital, with authority to act at his discretion as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 興宗即位，皇太后稱制，國事一委弟孝先。

translations.literal: When Xingzong took the throne, the Empress Dowager assumed regency; state affairs were wholly entrusted to her younger brother Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzong took the throne, the Empress Dowager assumed regency and entrusted all state affairs to her younger brother Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 方仁德皇后以馮家奴所誣被害，樸屢言其冤，不報。

translations.literal: Empress Rendu had been harmed through the false accusation of the Feng family slave; Pu repeatedly spoke of her injustice, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Rendu had been destroyed through a false accusation by the Feng family slave; Pu repeatedly spoke of her injustice, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 每念至此，為之嘔血。

translations.literal: Whenever he thought of this, he vomited blood for her sake.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he thought of it, he would vomit blood in grief.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，改王韓，拜東京留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he was transferred to Prince of Han and appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongxi he was transferred to Prince of Han and appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 及遷太后於慶州，樸徙王楚，升南院樞密使。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager was moved to Qing Prefecture, Pu was transferred to Prince of Chu and promoted to Southern Academy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager was moved to Qing Prefecture, Pu was transferred to Prince of Chu and promoted to commissioner of the Southern Academy.

sentences.zh: 四年，王魏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 薨，年五十，贈齊王。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty, and was posthumously granted Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged fifty, and was posthumously granted the title of Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 子鐸剌，國舅詳穩。

translations.literal: His son Duola was a detailed inspector of the empress's kin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duola served as detailed inspector of the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 耶律八哥，字烏古鄰，五院部人。

translations.literal: Yelu Bagge, style name Wugulin, was a man of the Five-Yuan Division.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Bagge, style name Wugulin, was a man of the Five-Yuan Division.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，書一覽輒成誦。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever; after one reading of a text he could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was clever; after a single reading he could recite a text from memory.

sentences.zh: 統和中，以世業為本部吏。

translations.literal: In the Tonghe era, through hereditary office he became an officer of his native division.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era, through hereditary office he became an officer of his native division.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升閘撒狘，尋轉樞密院侍御。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to zhasa mo, and soon was transferred to attendant of the Commission for Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to zhasa mo, and soon was transferred to attendant of the Commission for Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會宋將曹彬、米信侵燕，八哥以扈從有功，擢上京留守。

translations.literal: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Bagge, for meritorious service in the imperial retinue, was promoted to garrison commander of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Song generals Cao Bin and Mi Xin invaded Yan, Bagge, for meritorious service in the imperial retinue, was promoted to garrison commander of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 開泰四年，召為北院樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaitai he was summoned as deputy commissioner of the Northern Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaitai he was summoned as deputy commissioner of the Northern Academy.

sentences.zh: 頃之，留守東京。

translations.literal: Before long he was garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 七年，上命東平王蕭排押帥師伐高麗，八哥為都監，至開京，大掠而還。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Emperor ordered Eastern Pacification Prince Xiao Paiya to command an army against Goryeo; Bagge served as army supervisor; they reached Kaesong and returned after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Emperor ordered Eastern Pacification Prince Xiao Paiya to command an army against Goryeo; Bagge served as army supervisor; they reached Kaesong and returned after extensive plunder.

sentences.zh: 濟茶、陀二河，高麗追兵至。

translations.literal: At the Jicha and Tuo rivers, Goryeo pursuit troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jicha and Tuo rivers, Goryeo pursuit troops caught up with them.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆欲使敵渡兩河擊之，獨八哥以為不可，曰：「敵若渡兩河，必殊死戰，乃危道也；

translations.literal: The generals all wished to let the enemy cross the two rivers and then strike them; only Bagge thought this wrong and said: "If the enemy crosses the two rivers, they will fight to the death — that is a perilous course;
translations.idiomatic: The generals all wished to let the enemy cross the two rivers and then attack; only Bagge thought this unwise and said, "If the enemy crosses both rivers, they will fight to the death — that would be a perilous course;

sentences.zh: 不若擊於兩河之間。」

translations.literal: It would be better to strike them between the two rivers.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to attack them between the two rivers.

sentences.zh: 排押從之，戰，敗績。

translations.literal: Paiya followed this advice; they fought and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Paiya followed his advice; they gave battle and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 明年，還東京，奏渤海承奉官宜有以統領之，上從其言，置都知押班。

translations.literal: The next year, returning to the Eastern Capital, he memorialized that Bohai tribute-presenting officials ought to have someone to oversee them; the Emperor followed his advice and established the post of director of supervisory escort shifts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after returning to the Eastern Capital, he memorialized that Bohai tribute officials ought to be placed under unified supervision; the Emperor accepted his proposal and established the post of director of supervisory escort shifts.

sentences.zh: 後以茶、陀之敗，削使相，降西北路都監，卒。

translations.literal: Later, because of the defeat at Jicha and Tuo, he was stripped of commissioner rank, demoted to Northwestern Route army supervisor, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of the defeat at Jicha and Tuo, he was stripped of his commissioner rank, demoted to army supervisor of the Northwestern Route, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：張儉名符帝夢，遂結主知，服弊袍不易，誌敦薄俗，功著兩朝，世稱賢相，非過也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Zhang Jian's name matched the Emperor's dream, and thus he won the ruler's confidence; he wore a worn robe and would not change it, recording his devotion to plain custom; his achievements stood out in two reigns; the age calls him a worthy chief minister — this is no exaggeration.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Zhang Jian's name matched the Emperor's dream, and thus he won the ruler's trust; he wore a threadbare robe and would not replace it, bearing witness to his devotion to plain living; his achievements stood out across two reigns; the age calls him a worthy chief minister — and that is no exaggeration.

sentences.zh: 邢抱樸甄別守令，大愜人望，兩決滯獄，民無冤濫。

translations.literal: Xing Baopu distinguished competent from incompetent magistrates, greatly satisfying public expectation; twice he settled cases in arrears, and the people knew no wrongful punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Baopu distinguished competent from incompetent magistrates, greatly satisfying public expectation; twice he cleared long-pending cases, and the people suffered no wrongful punishment.

sentences.zh: 馬得臣引盛唐之治以諫其君，蕭樸痛皇后之誣，至於嘔血。

translations.literal: Ma Dechen cited the governance of High Tang to remonstrate with his ruler; Xiao Pu grieved over the calumny against the empress to the point of vomiting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dechen cited the governance of High Tang to remonstrate with his ruler; Xiao Pu grieved over the false accusation against the empress until he vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 四人者，皆以明經致位，忠藎若此，宜矣。

translations.literal: These four men all rose to office through mastery of the classics; such loyalty and earnestness as this was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: These four men all rose to office through mastery of the classics; such loyalty and earnest devotion as this was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 聖宗得人，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: In gaining such men, Shengzong's time was at its richest.
translations.idiomatic: In gathering such men, Shengzong's reign reached its fullest height.
